subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 27-year-old man is evaluated for exercise intolerance and muscle cramps during sports. Serum lactate is mildly elevated, and metabolic studies of his skeletal muscle mitochondria show slower oxidation of FADH2-linked substrates than of NADH-linked substrates.
question: Which of the following best explains the lower ATP yield from FADH2?

options.text: FADH2 donates electrons directly to complex I
Complex II does not pump protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane
FADH2 is oxidized in the cytosol rather than the mitochondrial matrix
Complex II generates GTP instead of ATP

explanation_correct: FADH2 transfers electrons to complex II, which lacks proton-pumping activity; electrons then pass through coenzyme Q, complex III, and complex IV. Because fewer protons are pumped into the intermembrane space, FADH2 yields about 1.5 ATP, whereas NADH yields about 2.5 ATP.

explanation_incorrect.A: FADH2 donates electrons at complex II, not complex I; NADH is the substrate for complex I.
explanation_incorrect.C: FADH2 is produced and oxidized in the mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane, not the cytosol.
explanation_incorrect.D: FADH2 electrons do pass through coenzyme Q after complex II; bypassing coenzyme Q is not the reason for the lower yield.
explanation_incorrect.E: Complex II does not produce GTP; GTP is generated by succinyl-CoA synthetase in the TCA cycle.

educationalObjective: Complex II does not pump protons, so FADH2 oxidation yields less ATP than NADH oxidation.
